scenes.headline: How Flash-dLLM caches keys that never sit still
scenes.sub: A fused KV-cache kernel, and a model that checks its own drafts
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cobble! Diffusion language models move every key and value, every step. Here's how Flash-dLLM caches them anyway.

scenes.text: Recompute a small window and the most-attended tokens in one fused kernel. Then let the model check its own drafts.

scenes.title: Why a diffusion cache goes stale

steps.label: Autoregressive: past keys never change
steps.say: An autoregressive model only looks back, so its cache is exact.

steps.label: Diffusion: every position reads every other
steps.say: A diffusion model looks both ways: commit one token and every key can move.

scenes.title: One layer of a cached step

left.title: Conventional cache path
items: Project, rotate, gather, attend: four kernels
left.say: The usual path runs four kernels per layer, each one round-tripping through memory.

right.title: Flash-Cache fused kernel
items: Write keys and values straight into the cache
right.say: Flash-Cache rotates on chip and writes straight into a flat cache: one point three seven times faster per layer.

steps.say: Each step recomputes sixteen decodable masks, plus forty-eight more as context.
Then the tokens just committed, and the decoded tokens the masks attend to most.
One fused kernel writes their keys and values. Every other row is reused.
Attention scores pick the next tracked set. There is no full refresh.

items.say: Draft the window, sorted by confidence.
Feed the rest back twice, as drafts and as masks.
Accept in order while both views agree. Stop at the first miss.

steps.say: The paper's own picture: tracked and masked tokens read the whole cache,
and drafts are checked against masked copies of themselves.

scenes.title: Tokens committed per step, GSM8K-512
scenes.note: LLaDA-1.5 with Flash-Cache, the paper's Table 6
scenes.say: On GSM8K, tokens per step go from two point eight to five point seven.

scenes.title: Throughput on GSM8K-512, tokens per second
scenes.say: Throughput: two hundred ten point six tokens a second, against forty-one point seven for Elastic-Cache.

scenes.text: A diffusion cache is always wrong somewhere. Keep the rows that matter fresh, and let the model vouch for its shortcuts.
scenes.mark: Keep the rows that matter fresh

recap: Recompute a window plus the most-attended tokens
Fuse projection, rotation and the cache write
Verify drafts against masked copies, same model
scenes.say: To recap: recompute a window and the busiest tokens, fuse the write, and let the model check its drafts.
